Subject: Confidentiality trigger — evidence & cap carve-out language request

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal at NovaMed are close to finalizing the order form, but Legal has a couple of non-negotiable asks around the liability cap for confidentiality/trade secret incidents. They want:

- A carve-out to the overall liability cap for losses arising from a confidentiality breach that meets the definition of a "trade secret" under applicable law.
- An evidence-first workflow and SLA for preservation/forensics — e.g., Redwood must preserve logs and provide initial evidence within 7 business days and full forensic report within 30 days for a qualifying incident.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept (1) a carve-out to the cap for trade-secret breaches and (2) the proposed evidence SLA above? If not, please propose alternate language and timing.

We intend to move to PO once legal gets comfortable. Attaching NovaMed's standard language for your reference.

Thanks,
Sasha Levin
Head of Procurement
NovaMed Health

Subject: Re: Confidentiality trigger — evidence & cap carve-out language request

Hi Sasha — appreciate the clarity. I've looped in Legal (Karthik) and Contracts (Marissa) to confirm. Quick summary from our side:

- We can consider a narrowly tailored carve-out to the liability cap for confirmed trade secret misappropriation where Redwood's systems are the proximate cause.
- We need to align on the threshold for what constitutes "confirmed" — NovaMed's proposed standard language implies a very low threshold (customer assertion + initial evidence). Redwood prefers a corroborated-forensics threshold before removing the cap.
- Evidence preservation SLAs are reasonable in principle, but we typically request a two-stage approach:
  1) Initial preservation confirmation within 3 business days (we pause deletion/retention policies and snapshot relevant logs).
  2) Delivery of a forensic intake report within 14 calendar days and a final report within 30–45 calendar days depending on complexity.

I've attached our redlines to the MSA and a proposed evidence-SLA matrix for alignment. Please let us know which parts are deal-breakers for NovaMed.

Next steps: Karthik, can you propose the exact carve-out wording and a brief note on evidentiary threshold? Marissa, can you confirm whether accepting the carve-out triggers any pricing/insurance requirements on our side?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Confidentiality trigger — evidence & cap carve-out language request

Folks — reading through NovaMed's proposed language and Neha's suggested approach. Proposed carve-out (draft language):

"Notwithstanding the limitation of liability set forth in Section X, the liability cap shall not apply to damages and equitable relief awarded as a result of (A) Redwood's material breach of its obligations under the Confidentiality provisions resulting in the misappropriation, unauthorized disclosure, or theft of Customer's information that qualifies as a trade secret under governing law, provided that Customer has: (i) notified Redwood promptly upon discovery; (ii) provided reasonable, corroborating evidence of trade-secret status; and (iii) permitted Redwood and its designated forensic vendor to conduct an investigation. For avoidance of doubt, the carve-out requires independent corroboration beyond a mere customer assertion."

Risk notes / rationale:
- We need the corroboration requirement to avoid subjective assertions escalating into uncapped liability.
- The carve-out should be limited to actual, demonstrable misappropriation (not mere accidental disclosure).
- Preserve ability to rely on third-party forensic vendor with mutually agreed scope and nondisclosure terms.

Evidence timeline (recommended):
- Preservation confirmation: within 3 business days of notification (snapshot & retention hold).
- Preliminary intake report: within 14 calendar days (scope, initial indicators, data retained).
- Final forensic report: within 30–45 calendar days depending on log volume / cooperation.

Operational ask: Can we add a clause that the customer must reimburse reasonable third-party forensic costs if the investigation shows the incident was caused by customer-side compromise or misuse? That helps prevent gaming.

I'll attach a redline with the exact text in track changes. Marissa — pricing/insurance implications?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: karthik_carveout_draft.docx (docx)
From: Sasha Levin <sasha@novamed.com>

Cc: Peter Chen <peter.chen@novamed.com>, legal@novamed.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Confidentiality trigger — evidence & cap carve-out language request

Thanks Karthik — helpful. A couple of clarifications from Legal:

- The corroboration requirement is acceptable if the MSA explicitly preserves Customer's right to seek interim equitable relief (injunctive relief) while forensics proceed.
- The vendor reimbursement ask is reasonable but we need an explicit burden-shifting standard: if Redwood's systems show compromise indicators (e.g., unauthorized egress from Redwood infra) then Redwood covers costs; if evidence points to customer-side compromise, NovaMed covers costs.
- The 14/30–45 day cadence is workable, but NovaMed requires an explicit commitment to provide a chain-of-custody and signed forensic statements suitable for regulatory audit (we operate in healthcare).

We can accept the carve-out language with those clarifications. Two remaining asks from procurement: 1) confirm Redwood will accept an exception to the cap solely for trade-secret misappropriation (not broader confidentiality breaches), and 2) confirm we can add a short notice-to-execute timeline (PO within 10 business days of final legal sign-off).

Sasha

Thanks, Sasha. Agreed on scope: Redwood will accept a narrowly tailored cap carve-out limited to confirmed trade-secret misappropriation (per the draft language Karthik provided) — not all confidentiality breaches. We'll add explicit interim equitable relief language and the chain-of-custody / signed statements commitment for healthcare audit needs.

On the vendor cost allocation: we'll accept the burden-shifting approach (Redwood pays where Redwood systems show indicators; NovaMed pays where evidence shows customer-side compromise), and we'll add mutual escalation and dispute-resolution steps for cost disagreements.

Marissa: once Karthik posts the final redline, can you push the order form acceptance through our approval queue and confirm whether any pricing uplift or insurance endorsement is required? If nothing material, we can proceed to DocuSign and the PO timeline Sasha requested (10 business days).
